To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NS1 protein is a useful diagnostic marker for dengue and Zika viruses, with a high degree of specificity for dengue virus.
the NS1 antigen is highly specific in the differential diagnosis of dengue and Zika virus infections.

the specificity of dengue NS1 antigen (Ag) was 99.9% in a cohort of dengue patients, 99.9–100% in a cohort from a dengue-endemic region, and 99.7% in a cohort that included patients with Zika virus infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a new method for the detection and quantification of the NS1 antigen of dengue in the serum of patients with suspected dengue infection.
the development of a rapid, sensitive, and specific diagnostic test for dengue and Zika virus infections.
the development of a novel method for the detection of dengue NS1 antigen in the differential diagnosis of dengue and Zika virus infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dengue virus infection can be ruled out with high probability if the NS1 antigen test is negative and the patient has a positive Zika virus RT-PCR result.

the dengue NS1 ELISA is not a good diagnostic tool for Zika virus infection, and the dengue virus-specific IgG ELISA should be used to confirm a Zika virus infection in the absence of dengue infection.
, at the time of this writing, the NS1 antigen test cannot be relied upon as the definitive diagnostic test for dengue virus infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dengue NS1 ELISA has a high sensitivity and specificity to detect dengue infection in the early phase of the disease.
the NS1 antigen test was specific for dengue and Zika virus infection.
the dengue NS1 antigen is a specific biomarker for dengue infection and that it is not detected in Zika virus–infected patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NS1 antigen is not a useful diagnostic tool for Zika virus infection in regions where dengue is endemic, because of the cross-reactivity with dengue virus NS1.
NS1 antigen detection is a useful tool for differential diagnosis of dengue and Zika virus infections, especially in areas with coexisting transmission of denguez and Zika viruses.
NS1 ELISA can be used to distinguish Zika and dengue infections in areas with active dengue transmission.
